newsitem.title: USA: Home Products Int'l Q1 net up after buy.
newsitem.headline: Home Products Int'l Q1 net up after buy.

text.p: Home Products International Inc said Tuesday its sales and earnings rose in the first quarter ended March 29 as demand for its plastic storage products continued to grow and its margins improved after an acquisition.

The company, formerly known as Selfix Inc, reported net income of $1.0 million, or $0.23 a share, compared to a loss of $22,000, or $0.01, last year. Sales totaled $31.7 million, up from $27.4 million a year ago.
Home Products said it restated earnings for all of 1996 to reflect its acquisition of Tamor Corp in December of last year, even though the deal actually closed February 28.
The company also said all five of its manufacturing plants are running at or above 100 percent of capacity, compared to 70 percent before the Tamor purchase.
Home Products shares were up 7/32 Tuesday at 10-3/8.
